thread:
ravi: Quick follow-up from the postmortem — thinking we should update the SLOs and track a remediation cadence. TL;DR: recurring latency spikes on token-gen path; error budget burned 45% last month. Thoughts?

katie: Agree we need changes. Do you propose tightening p95 or adding a throughput SLO?

ravi: My proposal: keep p50 target but tighten p95 from 400ms -> 300ms for the next quarter, and add a throughput SLO for 99th-percentile request rate to catch backpressure events. Also propose a monthly remediation cadence for long-lived items.

alex: +1 on cadence. For p95 change, we should simulate with current traffic shape first. Can we run a dashboard query to estimate expected burn?

sara: I can run the sim. Does p95 300ms refer to user-facing generation latency (token flush -> last token)? Confirm which metric.

ravi: Yes — metric is gen_request_latency_seconds{path="/v1/generate"} histogram p95 (end-to-end on inference nodes), excluding queue time. We'll need to update dashboard labels.

lee: If we tighten SLO we’ll likely hit error budget. Suggest a phased rollout: new SLO as a canary for 2 weeks in a secondary dashboard, then formalize if burn stays <40% for month.

katie: Proposed action items: 1) sara run sim and post projected burn by EOD Thu (owner: sara, due: Thu EOD) 2) alex update dashboard with secondary canary panel (owner: alex, due: Mon) 3) ravi draft SLO doc and remediation cadence (owner: ravi, due: Tue) 4) lee to add automation for monthly remediation reminders to the SLO board (owner: lee, due: next Wed).

oncall-bot: Incident 2026-03-18: auto-posted latency spike summary. Link: https://redwood/incident/2026-03-18

alex: Dashboard query I will use (promql):
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(gen_request_latency_seconds_bucket{path="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))
```
I'll duplicate the existing SLO panel to create a canary panel with 300ms threshold.

sara: Running the sim now against 30 days of traffic with current batching config. Initial result: projected p95 ~320ms under peak; with increased batching the projected p95 falls to ~290ms but costs change. I'll post numbers in a thread.

ravi: Good — include token distribution and queue time breakdown. Also include which deploys correlate with spikes (looks like large model rollouts).

lee: For remediation cadence, let's make a light-weight checklist per action item: owner, due date, rollback plan, test to validate. I can add a template to the SLO board.

katie: We should also add an alert rule that watches for recurring weekly spikes: if >3 spikes in 7d, auto-create a follow-up ticket assigned to the SLO owner.

alex: I'll add alert as a PagerDuty-triggering rule but only for the canary for 2 weeks so we don't spam.

ravi: OK timeline recap: sara results by Thu EOD; alex canary panel by Mon; ravi SLO draft by Tue; lee board automation by next Wed. We'll reconvene Fri 9am to sign off. If sims show p95 still >300ms we keep current SLO and focus on optimizations (caching, kv-prefix reuse, batching).

sara: Posted sim summary: p95 baseline 320ms; with batching tweak and kv-cache hit target to 85% -> 285ms; cost delta +8%. Link: https://redwood/notes/sim-1943123456

katie: Thanks. If cost delta OK, proceed with canary panel. I'll schedule the Friday 9am reconvene.

lee: Adding the monthly remediation cadence item to the SLO board and templating the checklist now.

ravi: Thanks everyone. I'll draft the SLO change RFC and include rollback thresholds for error budget (eg. if burn >60% in 14d revert to previous SLO).

katie: tiny nit — make sure dashboards tag by deployment-version so we can correlate model rollouts.

alex: Will do. Creating canary panel now.

ravi: Closing for now; follow-ups in the action items doc. :white_check_mark:
